chunks: A group narrated to us, from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani, from Abu Naeem Nasr ibn Isaam ibn al-Mughira al-Amri, from Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Naeem ibn Amr Qarqara al-Katib, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asadi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ismail ibn Ayyash, from Muhajir ibn Hakim, from Muawiyah ibn Saeed, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them), who said:

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: 'When two spears clash in al-Sham, it is a sign from the signs of Allah, the Exalted.' It was said: 'Then what?' He said: 'Then there will be an earthquake in al-Sham in which one hundred thousand will perish, which Allah will make a mercy for the believers and a punishment for the disbelievers. When that happens, look for the companions of the Barazin (red horses), and the yellow flags coming from the West until they settle in al-Sham. When that happens, await a subsidence (khurf) in a village of the villages of al-Sham called Harasta. When that happens, await the son of the liver-eater (Sufyani) from the valley of Yabis.'
ai.seo_question: What are the major signs of the end times in Syria according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Sufyani’s emergence as a pivotal eschatological event, linking the Syrian conflict and subsequent earthquake to divine retribution. The mention of 'yellow flags' (*al-ra'iyat al-sufraniyya*) specifically connects this sign to the Umayyad legacy, while the subsidence (*khasf*) in Harasta serves as a miraculous confirmation of his authority before his final defeat.
